judgements.justification: A's AC broke the visible 8/5/5 split with an emergency reviewer whose input is not on the forum and rejected 'based on this input and the discussions'.
Neither committee disputed clarity; both read the paper as clearly written.
The only score change, bYPA's 4 to 5 in B, came with a stated reason (evaluation concerns partly addressed).
A counted the silent xzpB's 5, but B had no silent detractor that its AC set aside; B's detractor bYPA engaged and was overruled on substance.
B had an invested champion (sJ2R, 8, ten hours), but A also had a reviewer rating 8 (TwiA), so the definition's 'no reviewer rating it that high' does not hold.
No reviewer said they read only part of the paper.
bYPA's domain-randomization reading was an objection to degree of novelty, not a contest of the paper's premise from another theoretical school, and it did not set B's outcome.
B's AC gave a stated case for the spotlight: a simple method of 'broad interest' with three enthusiastic accepts.

A's tdpf knew the ad hoc teamwork literature and checked novelty against Tylkin et al. and PLASTIC, while B's sJ2R could not judge the human-agent literature and B's AC called the details novel 'as far as I know'.
A's meta-review said 'several reviewers' raised limited novelty and no theory, but each came from one reviewer, and it omitted tdpf's 'not opposed to acceptance', in the direction of rejection.
No one in either committee raised narrow audience; B's AC called the paper of broad interest.
B's detractor bYPA was principled, not a misreading, and B's AC did weigh a higher tier and chose a spotlight.
The authors posted no new experiments on either forum; they told tdpf there was no time for further analysis.
A's highest-confidence reviewer, tdpf (confidence 4), rated 5, below the low-confidence 8; no expert review rated above the others.
No reviewer added a new objection or changed score after the response period; the late input was the AC's emergency reviewer, covered by R23.
Ratings tracked verbal assessments in both committees; praise-only reviews got 8 in A and 9 in B, and principled detractors got 5 in both.
tdpf's catch was a section heading ('highest scores across all maps'), not the paper's headline claim, and it played no part in A's rejection.
No committee converged on flat marginal-accept ratings; A rated 5, 8, 5 and B 9, 5, 8, 7, all at confidence 3 to 4.
